text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

Sex can't explain a difference between two candidates of the same sex. An all-woman panel chose a woman over you — another woman. Panel composition does nothing to explain why she was preferred, and raising it would damage your credibility with the one institution you may still want to work with or apply to again.

The real anomalies are elsewhere: a lower formal credential winning a licensed senior role, and a two-week silence on a reasonable request for written reasons. Those are worth pursuing. Send a polite follow-up to HR, citing the date of your original request and any policy or statutory right to feedback.

The likely story is a panel weighting community-facing skills, or an internal favourite — not your sex.
